<REPO>/tests/fixtures/antipatterns/label-collectors.html
  [hero-eyebrow-chip] eyebrow chip (tracked-caps) "Utah-based commercial insurance agency" above h1 "Commercial insurance that moves"
    → A tiny uppercase letter-spaced label sitting immediately above an oversized hero headline — or the same shape rendered as a pill chip — is now the default AI SaaS hero. Drop the eyebrow, integrate the kicker into the headline, or run it as a navigation breadcrumb instead.
  [cramped-padding] <div> "chip": children flush against border on top/bottom (no inset)
    → Text is too close to the edge of its container. Two shapes: (1) an element with its own text where the space between the rendered text and the border box is too small for the font size, and (2) a wrapper whose children's text lands flush against a visible boundary (border, outline, or non-transparent background) with nothing to inset it. Add at least 8px (ideally 12–16px) of space inside bordered, outlined, or colored containers.
  [cramped-padding] <div> "kicker-chip": children flush against bg on top/bottom (no inset)
    → Text is too close to the edge of its container. Two shapes: (1) an element with its own text where the space between the rendered text and the border box is too small for the font size, and (2) a wrapper whose children's text lands flush against a visible boundary (border, outline, or non-transparent background) with nothing to inset it. Add at least 8px (ideally 12–16px) of space inside bordered, outlined, or colored containers.
  [skipped-heading] <h1> "Two labels in one wrapper" followed by <h3> "A card that numbers itself" (missing h2)
    → Heading levels should not skip (e.g. h1 then h3 with no h2). Screen readers use heading hierarchy for navigation. Skipping levels breaks the document outline.

4 anti-patterns found.
